messages.content: Help me execute the `runIt` method to perform a test that includes creating an object of the tested class, invoking a method with a breakpoint, and logging the output to a `System.out` stream, using the arguments array `testArgs`?

function.name: clear001a_runIt
function.description: Executes a series of operations including creating an object of a tested class, invoking a method with a breakpoint, and logging the results to the provided PrintStream. Note that the provided function is in Java 8 SDK syntax.

args.description: An array of strings representing the arguments for the test. This is Java Array type parameter in string representation. The list elements are of type String; they are not in string representation.

out.description: The PrintStream to which the log messages will be written. This parameter can be of any type of Java object in string representation.

message.content:
Below is exactly what you have to send to the **tool** so that it creates the object, hits the breakpoint inside your target method, and writes everything into `System.out`.

```json
{
  "name": "clear001a_runIt",
  "arguments": {
    /* Replace the two placeholders below with whatever real data you actually want to feed */
    
    /* 1️⃣ Arguments passed to the tested method – expressed as a *Java* array literal.  
       Example: if your test needs “hello” and “world”, write:
          "args":"new String[]{\"hello\",\"world\"}"
       
       If you already have a local variable called `testArgs`, simply put its value here. */
    "args": "new String[]{\"yourArg0\",\"yourArg1\"}",  

    /* 2️⃣ Where the logs should go – we’re pointing at the standard console stream.  
       Using the fully‑qualified name keeps things unambiguous. */
    "out": "java.lang.System.out"
  }
}
```

### How it works

| Step | What happens |
|------|--------------|
| **Create instance** | Inside the tool’s implementation a fresh instance of the class under test is instantiated (`new TestedClass()` or similar). |
| **Invoke method + breakpoint** | It calls the designated method (`testedMethod`) while a debugger breakpoint is set right before/after the call. When the breakpoint fires, execution pauses until you resume it manually. |
| **Log result** | Whatever the method returns (or throws) gets printed through the supplied `PrintStream`. Because we gave `"java.lang.System.out"` the output appears straight in your console. |

> **Tip:** Make sure the JVM running the tool has debugging enabled (`-agentlib:jdwp=transport=dt_socket,address=*,server=y,suspend=n`). Otherwise the breakpoint won’t pause execution.

That’s all you need—just replace the placeholder arrays with your real test inputs and hit **Run**!
